summary.text: The external address ip-01 scanned and probed host-01, exploited its application as user-01 and opened a reverse shell back to ip-01. user-01 and then the privileged account user-02 were used from host-01 against host-02, and new services were installed on host-02 and host-03 by user-02.

claim.text: Reconnaissance and an exploit were followed by a reverse shell and new services on two more hosts, which fits backdoor installation after exploitation.

sequence.text: ip-01 scanned host-01 and probed its service versions.
An exploit request against the host-01 application ran as user-01.
A reverse shell connected from host-01 back to ip-01.
user-01 was used from host-01 against host-02.
The privileged account user-02 was used from host-01 on host-02.
New services were installed on host-02 and then on host-03 by user-02.

findings.text: A reverse shell from host-01 to ip-01 followed the exploit request within eight minutes.
The attacker moved from host-01 to host-02 and then used the privileged account user-02.
The services installed on host-02 and host-03 by user-02 are consistent with persistence.
The credentials of user-02 may have been taken on host-01; the events do not show how.

weaknesses.text: The application on host-01 accepted an exploit request from an external address.

impact.text: host-01, host-02 and host-03 may be under attacker control, including through the privileged account user-02.

recommendations.action: Review the new services on host-02 and host-03 and who created them.
recommendations.rationale: They were installed by user-02 right after the privileged account was used.
recommendations.reversible_alternative: Disable the services instead of deleting them, so they can be examined.

recommendations.action: Review recent use of user-01 and user-02 and consider resetting their credentials.
recommendations.rationale: Both accounts were used during the attack, user-02 with privileges.
recommendations.reversible_alternative: Require re-authentication at the next logon instead of a reset.

recommendations.action: Check the host-01 application for the exploited flaw and the reverse shell to ip-01.
recommendations.rationale: The chain started with an exploit request and a shell back to ip-01.
recommendations.reversible_alternative: Monitor traffic to ip-01 before blocking it.

risk_justification.text: The given high score fits an exploit, a reverse shell, use of a privileged account and new services on three hosts.

uncertainties.statement: The events do not show what the new services run.
uncertainties.missing_evidence: Service image paths and file hashes on host-02 and host-03.

uncertainties.statement: The events do not say whether each step succeeded.
uncertainties.missing_evidence: Outcome or action fields for each flagged event.

limitations: Host, IP and user values are pseudonymised tokens.
Three context events were given; they are treated as background only.
